html:
The Koryaks are a native people of the Russian Far East, living north of the Kamchatka Peninsula along the Bering Sea coast. The map shows them from 1530 to 1700. Their language is close to that of their northern neighbours, the Chukchi, within the Chukotko Kamchatkan family.

They had two ways of life. Inland Koryaks herded reindeer and moved with their herds across the tundra. Coastal Koryaks lived in settled villages and hunted seals, walrus and whales and fished for salmon. The two groups traded meat and hides for sea mammal fat and other goods.

Russian Cossacks reached their lands in the mid 1600s, as part of the Russian conquest of Siberia. The Koryaks resisted for decades, and fighting went on into the 1700s. They also often clashed with the Chukchi over reindeer. Their southern neighbours were the Itelmen of Kamchatka.
